message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Step | What Happens | Key Points | |------|--------------|------------| | **1. Setup** | • Shuffle the Uno deck (108 cards).
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | • If the first card is an action card, its effect applies to the first player. | | **2. Turn Order** | • Players take turns clockwise (or counterclockwise if a “Reverse” card is played). | • The direction changes with each Reverse. | | **3. Playing a Card** | • On your turn, you may play one card that matches either the **color** or the **number/symbol** of the top discard.
• You may also play a Wild card (any color) or a Wild Draw Four (any color + force next player to draw 4). | • If you have no playable card, you must draw from the draw pile. | | **4. Drawing a Card** | • If you draw a card that can be played immediately, you may play it on the same turn.
• If not, your turn ends. | • If the draw pile runs out, reshuffle the discard pile (except the top card) to form a new draw pile. | | **5. Action Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – Player chooses the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – Same as Wild, but next player draws four cards and loses their turn. | • Wild Draw Four can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise, the next player can challenge. | | **6. Winning a Turn** | • When you play your last card, shout “Uno!” before your next turn starts.
• If you forget, the next player can call you out and you must draw two cards. | • Failure to say “Uno” when you have one card left results in a penalty. | | **7. Winning the Game** | • The first player to reach a predetermined score (e.g., 500 points) wins.
• Points are tallied from the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | • After each round, players reset hands and deal again. | --- ### Quick Tips - **Keep track of colors** – It’s easier to play if you remember which colors are still in play. - **Use Wilds strategically** – Save them for when you’re stuck or to change the game’s momentum. - **Watch for challenges** – If you suspect a Wild Draw Four was played illegally, challenge it. The challenger must then draw four cards if the challenge fails. Enjoy playing Uno!
